review.why: Build production-quality, accessible, responsive UI: component structure, state choices, design system adherence and avoiding the generic AI look.
review.summary: Guidance for building interfaces: colocated component files, composition over configuration, a ladder for choosing state management, a table of AI-default looks to avoid, spacing and type scales, keyboard, ARIA and focus patterns, empty and error states, mobile-first layout, skeleton loading and optimistic updates, and a verification list.
strengths: Concrete code for the patterns that make UI feel finished: empty, loading and error states, focus management, optimistic updates.
The AI-aesthetic table names specific defaults (purple everything, oversized cards, stock grids) and what to do instead.
Tells the agent to verify with the project's own tooling and not to install toolchains just to check its work.
cautions: Generic across frameworks: examples are React and Tailwind flavored, with no framework-specific rules.
Links to an accessibility checklist outside the skill folder that a single-skill install does not include.
Read in full but not run here.
